overall: The AG found the Dighton-Rehoboth Regional School Committee did not violate the Open Meeting Law: notices were sufficient, no outside deliberation was shown, and counsel's authority/re-vote claims were declined as non-OML issues.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the committee voted on a district-wide 'tent meeting' budget vote at its Sept 30 or Oct 17 meetings without posting notice of that topic.
allegations.key_passage: Because the Committee did not vote to authorize the “tent meeting” at either the September 30 or October 17 meetings, we find that the Committee did not violate the Open Meeting Law by failing to include that topic on its meeting notices.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Oct 17 notice 'Continued discussion of the FY20 budget' was too vague to cover the tent meeting discussion held that night.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, as the notice informed the public that the Committee would be discussing the FY20 Budget, and that is in fact what was discussed, the notice was sufficiently detailed to comply with the Open Meeting Law in this respect.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged members deliberated outside a posted meeting when choosing the tent meeting date and venue and drafting the warrant language and notice letter.
allegations.key_passage: We find no evidence of deliberation outside of a posted meeting.

allegations.summary: Town counsel asserted the committee had to re-vote to re-authorize the tent meeting after July 18 and lacked authority to call it without another vote on the warrant.
allegations.key_passage: We note that, even if true, these allegations would not constitute a violation of the Open Meeting Law, G.L. c. 30A, §§ 18-25.
